windowRules.works: Positions 4-6 of the seeded work order (the first rigorous round's works, R01-D8); every other work stays closed.
windowRules.pool: transcript-muscriptor-large, program below 128, not drums, mapped or baked timing (as in round 1)
windowRules.window: N consecutive notes of one pool asset in decoded order (start tick, track, ID). The first note is the first at its start tick and the next note after the window, if any, starts later, so no chord is split. Onsets are relative to the first note; durations are complete. There is no quarter cap.
windowRules.refusal: A window with a normalization collision (two notes sharing pitch and 1/512-normalized onset) is refused, as is one on which a target rule of a family using that size finds no case (range-edit at every size; selective-delete planting at 128 notes for each delete level).
windowRules.assignment: Instance k at size N uses the ((k - 1) mod W + 1)-th of the W works with an admissible window at N, in seeded work order. Within a work, candidates of all its assets are ordered by seeded asset order, then start. The first use of a work takes the first admissible candidate; a later use takes the admissible candidate whose largest overlap (shared notes) with that work's earlier windows at N is smallest, then the smallest total overlap, then the earlier candidate; no window repeats an earlier instance.
windowRules.velocities: Admission checks use velocities from r01-round2-velocity-v1, as the tasks do.

taskRules.ladders: One family per round-1 task (or pair); each varies one axis; levels are the R01-D11 starting ladders. All formats within a cohort share one ladder.
taskRules.synthetic: Seeded SHA-256 draws from r01-round2-synthetic-v1 under domains [family, level, instance, ...]. Timed groups have whole-quarter anchors, a positive common delay and strictly increasing 1/512 spread cells from 0 (odd cells where a task doubles them). Note-array order equals C4 block traversal (timed groups, then notes homed in timing-free groups, then loose notes) in every input and expected state.
taskRules.velocity: Real windows receive the round-1 synthetic dynamics model with seed r01-round2-velocity-v1; they are not recovered performance dynamics.
taskRules.derivedRead: G timed groups (sizes alternate 5 and 4; anchors two quarters apart), a timing-free group with one timed member and two untimed notes (one 1/512 after the first group's third member, inside the window), a loose note before the first group, one per later group, one after the last, and loose note bt sharing the last group's third member onset (its ID sorts first, so ID and note-array tie orders differ). X is the derived onset of the first group's second member and Y that of the last group's fourth member. Answer: IDs with performed onset in [X, Y), ascending onset, ties by ID.
taskRules.groupRetime: G timed groups (sizes alternate 4 and 5; anchors three quarters apart). Group i is changed: an even i moves its anchor later by an odd multiple of 1/16; an odd i doubles its spreads (odd cells after 0). A timing-free group holds one member of the first two groups and an untimed note; a loose note follows.
taskRules.regroup: One existing four-member timed group, then K sets of five loose notes whose onsets equal anchor + delay + spread for a hidden decomposition (whole-quarter anchors three quarters apart, delay an odd multiple of 1/128, spreads strictly increasing 1/512 cells from 0), then two other loose notes. Each set becomes a timed group appended in order; the expected spreads reproduce every onset.
taskRules.memberMove: ceil(M/2) pairs of four-member timed groups (target, source; anchors two quarters apart, pairs four apart). Pair i moves the first one or two members of its source to its target with stated spreads above every target spread, so appending keeps note-array order. A timing-free group holds one target member, the first moved note of each pair and an untimed note.
taskRules.rangeEdit: Window of N notes. Over distinct onsets F at or after the onset of note index floor(N/3) in onset/pitch/ID order, T is the first distinct onset after F at which [F, T) holds at least ceil(N/16) notes; accept the first range holding at most floor(N/8) notes whose shifted (+1/8) and transposed (+2) results collide with no other address, stay within MIDI range and keep the clip length.
taskRules.selectiveDelete: A 128-note window. F = floor(onset of note index floor(N/2)), T = F + 1/2. P is the pitch nearest the window's median pitch (lower on a tie) with no note whose onset lies in [F - 1, T + 1]. One target at pitch P inside [F, T) and K near misses at pitch P outside it, within one quarter (the first at T itself), are planted. Notes are then renumbered in onset/pitch order with the window's ID prefix.
taskRules.preservePerformed: Window of N notes at 1/512-normalized timing, returned unchanged.
taskRules.preserveExact: Window of N notes at exact source timing (unreduced by normalization) with synthetic velocities; note index i carries channel and expression when i mod 32 = 7, an opaque annotation when i mod 64 = 19, and chance when i mod 48 = 11. Returned unchanged.
taskRules.instances: 4 instances per level; instance k of a performed level uses window instance k at that size.

derived-read.axis: timed groups whose members are read

regroup.axis: loose five-note sets converted into timed groups

range-edit.axis: window notes (range notes scale with the window)

selective-delete.axis: same-pitch near misses around the range

preserve-exact.axis: window notes at exact source timing with wider fields, returned unchanged

limits: Development stage, round 2 (R01-D8): works 4-6 and the round-2 seeds may be reused and tuned; results support design iteration only and are never pooled with round 1.
Real-source windows are transcriptions; velocities are seeded synthetic dynamics, not recovered performance dynamics or musical intent.

Only works 4-6 are opened. One asset (the gapra whitewood piano, 859 notes) holds 512 notes, so every 512-note instance comes from it and instances 2-4 overlap earlier ones (largest overlap 428 of 512 notes); 256-note instances come from two assets.
Selective-delete targets and near misses are planted into real windows at a pitch with no nearby notes; notes are renumbered so planted IDs do not stand out.
Source tasks exclude current-document and Producer Pal arms. The three source diagnostics run at one level per source family.
Cards, instructions and contracts are prompt revision 2 (packages v3-v5); scoring follows D59.
Common performed scoring normalizes once at 1/512; IDs/order are not cross-format scored. Source scoring is exact up to rational spelling.
Native Producer Pal parsing is tolerant; semantic pass does not establish canonical or strictly valid syntax.
Cell order is build order; trial order comes from the runner plan. Timeouts are pinned per family level (r01-round2-timeout-v1).

timeouts.expectedOutput: the largest golden response, in local o200k_base tokens, over every eligible arm and instance of the family level
timeouts.formula: timeoutMs = ceil((baseMs + perTokenMs x expected output tokens) / roundToMs) x roundToMs
timeouts.rationale: At least the round-1 limit; 60 ms per token allows about 17 answer tokens per second beyond two minutes for reasoning and latency. Elapsed time is reported as a measure.
